ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.44 (voucher, NS-7) to the rider for the unexempted 1.73 km off-route segment; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file; no account flag.

segment_findings.reason: The only pre-segment rider message F8 (21:44) accepted the driver's F7 (21:43) request to 'pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute' — a stop for a purpose, not a road, area or route named for travel. RD-5 consent therefore does not extend to the 1.73 km off-route leg driven to reach it [F7][F8][F3][RD-5]. The rider named no place, so RD-3(a) is not satisfied; the driver chose the point that produced the off-route segment, so RD-3(b) applies and the extra km is not exempted by the stop request [F8][F3][RD-3]. No RD-4 incident or band 1/2 record supports exemption [F13][F11][F12][RD-4]. The extra km are refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Timing is satisfied (F8 21:44 precedes the segment start 21:47 in F3), but RD-5 requires the consent to cover the segment: F7 named a petrol station stop, not a road/area/route, so the 1.73 km off-route leg is outside the admitted scope [F7][F8][F3][RD-5].

The consent cannot rest on the driver's post-trip statement F10; under G11 a driver's claim of agreement is not consent, and F8 names no place or route [F10][F8][RD-5]. RD-3(a) requires a rider-named place, which is absent [F8][F3][RD-3].
RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 before a flag; F16 shows 0 upheld route disputes, so no account action attaches even though the refund is positive [F16][RD-6].
F16 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so this case cannot make the conduct 'repeated' under RD-6; no flag_account [F16][RD-6].

Correct that a segment exists (F3), and it is unexempted, but it is not 'unexplained': the rider was told of and agreed to a stop at 21:43–21:44 [F7][F8][RD-1]. Only the extra kilometres, not the whole deviation as misconduct, are refunded under RD-2 [F3][RD-2].

what_would_change: F3: if the judge finds the rider agreed to this route or named this stop beforehand, it is exempt; if not, $2.44 is refunded; if the record cannot settle it, a person decides.
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.
